key_insight: THz time-domain spectroscopy can non-destructively fingerprint specific grain-boundary defect species in organic halide perovskites and quantify them via spectral oscillator strength.
engineering_relevance: This enables closed-loop defect screening and passivation guidance for higher-efficiency, more stable perovskite solar cells without contact-based damage or ambiguity.
method: Measure 0.3–3.0 THz spectra of device-relevant perovskite thin films
Identify intrinsic phonons and grain-boundary-localized defect vibrations across multiple compositions
Build a THz defect library and use oscillator-strength analysis for quantitative defect mapping
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the 1.58 THz absorption in SVE-grown MAPbI3 scales linearly with XPS-quantified CH3NH2 defect concentration, supporting THz-TDS as a direct defect meter.
watch_item: The approach depends on a composition-specific THz fingerprint library, so extending it to new materials or overlapping defect signatures may require additional calibration and validation.
paper_title: Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy as a Universal Defect Fingerprinting Tool for Organic Halide Perovskite Solar Cells
